first_impression.reaction: Santorini, all those cliffs and steps. That's what I picture before anything else. The opening is calm and to the point: four areas, and the choice depends on guest numbers and the ceremony. Nobody is gushing at me. I'll read it properly, top to bottom.

journey.quote: Greek summers bring frequent heatwaves and a wildfire season from June to September, and Santorini sits in an active seismic zone, so plan shade, timing and a fallback for your date.
journey.reaction: Good. Heat, fires and earthquakes right at the top, not buried. That tells me they aren't trying to sell me a postcard.

journey.section: Santorini wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: | Venue | Area | Caldera view setting | Ceremony options | Largest published capacity |
journey.reaction: I had to slide it sideways on the iPad, and with so many 'Not published' boxes I'm not sure what I'm comparing. I'll look at it with my husband on the big screen.

journey.section: How to compare Santorini venues like for like
journey.quote: Anything this guide marks "Not published", from capacity to exclusive use, needs an answer in writing before you commit, and your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you sign
journey.reaction: In writing, before we sign, and someone named whose job it is to check. That's the accountability I want for this kind of money.

journey.quote: Grace requires a wedding planner for every wedding, engaged at least three months before the day, and the wedding party has a private lounge from 8am.
journey.reaction: Glad that's said plainly. That's the kind of rule you find out about too late and then pay for twice.

journey.quote: Not published: ceremony types, capacity, room count, exclusive use.
journey.reaction: By the fourth or fifth venue these lines all run together and I started skimming them. Honest, I suppose, but a bit tiring.

journey.quote: For guests with limited mobility, Le Ciel is the one venue here that publishes step-free access.
journey.reaction: That's the line I'd read to my husband. Ramps and very few steps. Mum and her walking frame are the first thing I think of on a cliff island. Only one out of thirteen, though, which worries me about the rest.

journey.section: Getting to Santorini for your wedding
journey.quote: It has Schengen and non-Schengen departure areas, a public bus and taxis, and an accessible travel service for passengers with reduced mobility.
journey.reaction: An assistance service at the airport is reassuring. But I'm not putting an 88-year-old on a public bus or in a taxi queue. Who arranges a proper car for her?

journey.section: Getting to Santorini for your wedding
journey.quote: Older guests should know about the stairs before they book. Ask each venue how many steps lie between the road, the rooms and the ceremony space.
journey.reaction: Thank you. They've thought about people like my mother without me having to sound fussy for raising it.

journey.quote: Greece is in an active seismic zone with earthquakes and volcanic activity, including near Santorini.
journey.reaction: I appreciate the honesty, but that gives me a jolt. It doesn't say what happens if something does occur around the date, or what insurance the family should take out. That's where I'd want a person to talk me through it.

journey.quote: Agree a covered or indoor fallback with your venue in advance.
journey.reaction: Sensible. I like that it plans for the bad day as well as the sunset.

journey.quote: Ask the Greek embassy or consulate whether you need one, whether you can get it in Australia, and whether it needs an authentication or apostille.
journey.reaction: Clear enough, and dated government advice. I still can't tell whether my daughter does all this herself or whether the Advisor handles it with her.

journey.quote: How many steps lie between the road, the rooms and the ceremony space, and is there a step-free route?
journey.reaction: A proper numbered list I can print and hand to my daughter. The access question being on it is exactly right.

journey.section: Shortlist your Santorini venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: One person, Australian time, AUD, the fee in writing. That's the paragraph my husband needs to see. I'd still want a phone call before a cent changes hands.

unanswered_questions: Apart from Le Ciel, which of these cliff venues can a guest with a walking frame actually get around, from the room to the ceremony terrace?
Who arranges a private transfer from the airport for older guests, rather than the bus or a taxi queue?
What travel and medical insurance should older guests carry, given the heat, wildfires and earthquakes mentioned?
Who prepares and lodges the legal paperwork in practice: my daughter, the venue or the Wedded Advisor?
Is the venue deposit protected, and who reads a contract written in Greek and in euros?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong at 2am Santorini time?
Is the first step a phone call with the Wedded Advisor, before anything is booked or paid?
would_share_with: My husband, with the closing section (fee in writing, AUD, one person) and the Le Ciel step-free line
My daughter, with the booking checklist, especially the access and weather fallback questions
My sister, who is looking after Mum on the trip, with the stairs, ferry and heat advice

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
cta_reaction.why: A named person, our time zone, AUD and the fee in writing tick most of my boxes. I'd click if it said plainly that a real person rings me first, before anything is booked, and that they'd check which venues my mother can get around.

top_3_changes: Add step-free access to the things the Wedded Advisor confirms in writing (the primary CTA line), so the mobility question has someone accountable for it on a cliff island.

After the earthquake, wildfire and heat advice, add one plain line telling families to arrange travel and medical insurance that suits older guests, and mention organised transfers alongside the bus and taxis.
Say in one plain sentence who does the legal paperwork in practice (the couple, with the Advisor's help or not), and trim the per-venue 'Not published' lines where they repeat the table.

HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible

open_questions.question: Accessibility is handled better than Mykonos (stairs warning, checklist item, Le Ciel step-free), but only one of 13 cliff venues answers it. Insurance and organised transfers remain gaps. Treat as should-fix? Deposit, contract language and on-the-day contact are deferred business details.

assumptions: Margaret reads the whole article on an iPad because her daughter sent it, and her own mother uses a walking frame (per voice samples).
Prices are deliberately not printed, so their absence was not raised.
